title: John 10:22–42
context: At the Feast of Dedication, the Jews press Jesus to say plainly whether he is the Christ. He replies that he has told them and that his works bear witness, but they do not believe because they are not among his sheep. His sheep hear his voice and follow him. He gives them eternal life, they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of his hand or the Father’s. He and the Father are one. When they try to stone him for blasphemy, he appeals to Scripture and his works, then withdraws beyond the Jordan, where many believe. Verses 26–29 are a key text in the debate over election and eternal security.

verses.text: It was the Feast of the Dedication at Jerusalem.
verses.arminianNotes: It was the Feast of Dedication in Jerusalem. Arminian readers note the setting, recalling God’s deliverance in the time of the Maccabees.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see Jesus as the true temple, revealed at a feast celebrating the temple’s rededication.

verses.text: It was winter, and Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon’s porch.
verses.arminianNotes: It was winter, and Jesus was walking in Solomon’s colonnade. Arminian readers see John’s eyewitness detail.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the historical setting of a decisive confrontation.

verses.text: The Jews therefore came around him and said to him, “How long will you hold us in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.”
verses.arminianNotes: “If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.” Arminian readers see a demand that reflects resistance more than openness.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see unbelief that would not accept any answer.

verses.text: Jesus answered them, “I told you, and you don’t believe. The works that I do in my Father’s name, these testify about me.
verses.arminianNotes: I told you, and you do not believe. The works I do bear witness. Arminian readers see sufficient evidence refused.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see that evidence alone does not produce faith.

verses.text: But you don’t believe, because you are not of my sheep, as I told you.
verses.arminianNotes: You do not believe because you are not among my sheep. Arminian readers see “not my sheep” as describing their character and settled unbelief, not a decree that made belief impossible.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the order of the verse: not being a sheep is the reason for unbelief, not the result. Being a sheep comes first.
verses.keyContrast: Both see unbelief connected to not being Christ’s sheep. Arminian readers see “not my sheep” as describing persistent unbelief. Reformed readers see belonging to the sheep as prior to and the cause of believing.

verses.text: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.
verses.arminianNotes: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. Arminian readers stress that the sheep are those who keep hearing and following, so the description is ongoing.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the marks of those who belong to Christ, which flow from his knowledge of them.

verses.text: I give eternal life to them. They will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand.
verses.arminianNotes: I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand. Arminian readers affirm that no outside power can snatch believers from Christ. They hold that this does not stop a believer from walking away by ceasing to follow (v27).
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see an absolute promise of eternal security. Those who receive eternal life will never perish, and no one, including the believer, can remove them.
verses.keyContrast: Both affirm that no one can snatch Christ’s sheep from his hand. Arminian readers see protection from outside forces for those who keep following. Reformed readers see an unconditional guarantee that Christ’s sheep will never perish.

verses.text: My Father who has given them to me is greater than all. No one is able to snatch them out of my Father’s hand.
verses.arminianNotes: My Father, who has given them to me, is greater than all, and no one is able to snatch them out of the Father’s hand. Arminian readers see the Father’s power protecting those who remain his sheep.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the double grip of Father and Son, which makes the believer’s security certain.

verses.text: I and the Father are one.”
verses.arminianNotes: I and the Father are one. Both traditions see a profound claim to unity with the Father. Arminian readers see that unity guaranteeing the Father’s and Son’s shared care for believers.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see a statement of the Son’s deity, the ground of the believer’s security.

verses.text: Therefore the Jews took up stones again to stone him.
verses.arminianNotes: The Jews picked up stones again to stone him. Arminian readers see violent rejection of Jesus’ claim.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see that they understood him to claim deity.

verses.text: Jesus answered them, “I have shown you many good works from my Father. For which of those works do you stone me?”
verses.arminianNotes: For which good work are you going to stone me? Arminian readers see Jesus appealing to the evidence of his works.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see Jesus exposing the irrationality of unbelief.

verses.text: The Jews answered him, “We don’t stone you for a good work, but for blasphemy, because you, being a man, make yourself God.”
verses.arminianNotes: “You, being a man, make yourself God.” Both traditions see Jesus’ opponents recognizing his claim to deity. Arminian readers note that they understood him clearly.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the charge as confirming that Jesus claimed equality with God.

verses.text: Jesus answered them, “Isn’t it written in your law, ‘I said, you are gods’?
verses.arminianNotes: “Is it not written in your Law, ‘I said, you are gods’?” Arminian readers see Jesus arguing from Psalm 82.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see an argument from lesser to greater, not a denial of his unique deity.

verses.text: If he called them gods, to whom the word of God came (and the Scripture can’t be broken),
verses.arminianNotes: If he called them gods to whom the word of God came, and Scripture cannot be broken. Both traditions see “Scripture cannot be broken” as a strong statement of Scripture’s authority.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the verse as a key support for the infallibility of Scripture.

verses.text: do you say of him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, ‘You blaspheme,’ because I said, ‘I am the Son of God’?
verses.arminianNotes: Do you say of him whom the Father consecrated and sent, “You are blaspheming”? Arminian readers see Christ’s unique sending.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the Son consecrated for his mission.

verses.text: If I don’t do the works of my Father, don’t believe me.
verses.arminianNotes: If I am not doing the works of my Father, do not believe me. Arminian readers see Jesus inviting examination of the evidence.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the works as testimony to the Son’s divine mission.

verses.text: But if I do them, though you don’t believe me, believe the works, that you may know and believe that the Father is in me, and I in the Father.”
verses.arminianNotes: Believe the works, that you may know that the Father is in me and I am in the Father. Arminian readers see Jesus urging faith even from those resisting him.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the works pointing to the mutual indwelling of Father and Son.

verses.text: They sought again to seize him, and he went out of their hand.
verses.arminianNotes: They sought to arrest him, but he escaped. Arminian readers see that his hour had not yet come.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God’s sovereign timing protecting Jesus until his appointed hour.

verses.text: He went away again beyond the Jordan into the place where John was baptizing at first, and he stayed there.
verses.arminianNotes: He went away again across the Jordan. Arminian readers see Jesus withdrawing from hostility.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see providence guiding his movements.

verses.text: Many came to him. They said, “John indeed did no sign, but everything that John said about this man is true.”
verses.arminianNotes: Many came to him and said, “Everything John said about this man was true.” Arminian readers see John’s witness bearing fruit.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God using the testimony of his servants to bring people to faith.

verses.text: Many believed in him there.
verses.arminianNotes: Many believed in him there. Arminian readers see people responding in faith when the evidence is weighed honestly.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God gathering his sheep, in contrast with the unbelief in Jerusalem.
